title: When the Guard Adds Nothing: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for LLM‑Produced Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=300 task pairs) that measured whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline increases the probability that an LLM‑produced vendor CLI configuration passes a conservative deterministic validator, compared to direct LLM generation. The preregistration froze a shared‑initial candidate per task (one generator call shared by both arms) and a bounded guarded policy that allows at most one automatic repair call if the shared initial failed. Under the declared prompt and generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini), every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator (baseline = 300/300; guarded = 300/300). The preregistered paired test yields n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10k resamples, seed = 1729). Because no initial failures occurred, the preregistered single‑repair policy was not invoked. All execution artifacts (task manifest, model configuration, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, analysis inputs/outputs) are archived and hash‑signed to enable exact reproduction.

sections.introduction: Generative models that translate operator intent into vendor CLI changes promise to reduce operator effort but raise operational risk unless outputs are validated before application. A common mitigation architecture is generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R): an LLM generator proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator enforces syntactic and workflow invariants, and an automatic repair stage attempts bounded corrections when the validator fails. We preregistered a tightly scoped confirmatory design that isolates the marginal effect of a bounded, single automatic repair on a fixed candidate: for each task we shared the same initial generator output between the two arms (baseline vs guarded) and allowed the guarded arm one deterministic repair call only when that initial candidate failed the validator. The core research question is: under this shared‑initial protocol, does a one‑step automatic repair increase the per‑task probability of producing a validator‑passing configuration relative to direct generation? Our contributions are artifactized and reproducible: (1) a machine‑readable preregistration (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; SHA‑256 = a85d66d4c6ce2275e2d8c820f96c610532dbb5452bebb3fe108848f9dc38cdf6), (2) a curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest and deterministic validator with full execution traces, (3) a confirmatory paired analysis with exact statistics and bootstrap CIs computed from the archived artifacts, and (4) a public artifact bundle (manifest and per‑episode hashes) enabling exact replay.
sections.related_work: Intent‑to‑configuration and intent‑driven NetOps have seen many recent proposals that couple natural language translation with verification (e.g., Nguyen et al., 2024; Chakraborty et al., 2024; Mondal et al., 2025). Deterministic verification and SMT/SMT‑based approaches for network policy verification (Bagpipe / Weitz et al., 2016) are canonical references for validator design. Benchmarks and pipeline artifacts for LLMs in NetOps (NetLLMBench; UniAIOps) motivated our manifest, and recent tool‑augmented self‑refinement and constrained repair frameworks (INTERACSPARQL, LATCH) motivated a bounded single‑repair policy. We cite only verified primary sources and provide canonical artifact paths and SHA‑256 values for the manifests and analysis used in this study (see Cited Record Ids and the reproducibility section below).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The design and analysis plan are frozen in the preregistration (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; SHA‑256 = a85d66d4c6ce2275e2d8c820f96c610532dbb5452bebb3fe108848f9dc38cdf6) and were not changed after observing results. Task manifest and validator. The task manifest is a curated 300‑task multi‑vendor intent corpus limited to vendor CLI fragments with explicit safe‑sequence constraints and required final states; canonical manifest path: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) applies parsing, canonicalization, syntactic checks, interface assignment invariants, required ordering patterns (e.g., make‑before‑break, down‑before‑change when required), and destructive‑pattern detection. Execution contract. The execution adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1 operating in scientific_confirmatory mode with the declared model snapshot gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). The preregistered call budget allowed at most one shared initial generation per task and at most one repair call for the guarded arm if the shared initial failed; maximum_model_calls = 600 (planned), actual model_calls_used = 300 (one shared initial per task). Inclusion/exclusion and missingness. Inclusion rules, retry policy for transient provider errors, and contamination detection (exact/fuzzy matching and high‑entropy token heuristics) were preregistered and executed. All raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, and per‑episode hashes are archived and listed in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json and the artifact hash lists under execution/*; representative examples are cited below). Analysis plan. The primary test is an exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes with a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) as pre‑specified. Secondary per‑vendor paired comparisons were pre‑specified with Bonferroni correction (family alpha = 0.05). All analysis inputs and outputs are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0).
sections.results: Execution bookkeeping. The run executed the full preregistered manifest: planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 600; failed episodes = 0. Provider calls: 300 completed hosted model call events (one shared initial generation per task); cache hits = 0; cache misses = 300 (detailed provider traces archived under execution/provider_calls/, e.g., execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json SHA‑256 = a59191a39575bd602217f53eac4f3e5c6ef03b203d3dd678edcb06f8964e5e49). Confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded numbers). The deterministic per‑episode scoring files show that every shared initial candidate passed the validator without repairs: baseline_success_count = 300/300; guarded_success_count = 300/300. The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Repair activity. Because there were zero initial validator failures in every task, the guarded arm never invoked the preregistered single automatic repair; repair call count = 0. Representative episode traces. Example archived scoring traces with validator diagnostics and canonicalized configurations include execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d0...), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...), and the full per‑episode shards are listed and hash‑signed in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation. The paired design compares outcomes on identical initial candidates shared across arms; its power to detect repair benefit depends on the generator producing at least some initial failures (discordant pairs). Here the generator + prompt + model snapshot produced a ceiling outcome: every shared initial candidate satisfied the deterministic validator, eliminating discordance and making the primary paired test uninformative for repair effect (no discordant pairs exist to attribute repair benefit). The observed paired difference is exactly 0.00 and the two‑sided McNemar p = 1.00; the paired bootstrap CI collapses to [0.00, 0.00] because of zero discordance. This is an artifact‑grounded factual outcome, not a null‑result by post‑hoc selection: the preregistered artifacts and analysis logs (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 7bc0bb7d...) record the finished run and the exact numeric outputs. Reviewer request regarding per‑vendor secondary tests. The preregistration pre‑specified per‑vendor paired secondary tests. We executed the confirmatory analysis exactly as specified and found zero discordant pairs overall and therefore within every vendor subgroup; in that situation per‑vendor paired McNemar tests cannot produce meaningful differences. The canonical task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3) contains vendor labels for every task and is the authoritative source for computing any subgroup counts; auditors can compute vendor distributions and subgroup tables programmatically from that manifest. To avoid reporting unverified subgroup counts, we state clearly that the preregistered per‑vendor paired tests were not informative because no discordant pairs were observed in any subgroup. Operational implications and follow‑ups. The empirical lesson is simple and bounded: for this prompt/model snapshot and this curated 300‑task manifest, a conservative deterministic validator accepted every shared initial candidate, so a bounded one‑repair remediation step did not produce additional validator passes. This does not imply automatic repair is universally unnecessary. Follow‑ups to probe regimes where repair may help include (a) increasing task hardness or adversariality, (b) switching to independent initial draws per arm (remove the shared‑initial constraint), (c) increasing repair budget (iterative repair attempts), or (d) evaluating different model snapshots or prompt templates. All artifacts in this run support exact replay and controlled perturbations: change the manifest, prompt, or model identifier and re‑run the preregistered pipeline to map when repairs add measurable value. Reproducibility and artifact accounting. Every principal artifact is archived and hash‑signed. Representative canonical artifacts and their SHA‑256 values are: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d0...), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...), and the full execution manifest enumerates the complete hash list. The preregistration path and SHA are provided above. Limitations (artifact‑grounded) and scope cautions follow.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that isolated the marginal effect of a bounded single automatic repair on a shared LLM candidate across 300 multi‑vendor NetOps intents. Under the declared prompt and gpt‑5‑mini snapshot every shared initial candidate passed our conservative deterministic validator, so the preregistered single‑repair policy was never invoked and produced no measurable benefit (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00]). The empirical result is narrow and artifact‑anchored: when the declared generator configuration already produces validator‑passing outputs on the chosen task distribution, adding a bounded repair stage does not increase deterministic pass rates but adds cost. All artifacts (preregistration, task manifest, model configuration, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis inputs/outputs) are archived and hash‑signed to support exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups that vary prompt, model snapshot, task hardness, or repair budget.

limitations: Single model snapshot (gpt-5-mini) evaluated — results do not generalize to other models or model versions.

Deterministic validator implements a conservative subset of operational hazards (syntactic checks, interface and workflow invariants) and omits dynamic/emulation‑level checks and deeper routing semantics.

Curated 300‑task manifest may not include adversarial or out‑of‑distribution failure modes; under the chosen prompt and model snapshot every shared initial candidate passed the validator (ceiling effect), limiting the ability to measure G‑V‑R improvements under the preregistered one‑repair policy.

Shared initial‑candidate design (preregistered) fixes the same initial generation for both arms to isolate repair effect; this reduces sensitivity to generator variability and can mask repair value when the generator is already accurate on the task set.
Only a single automatic repair attempt was permitted per task; iterative or human‑in‑the‑loop repair policies were not evaluated.
Automated contamination detection cannot eliminate memorization risk entirely; the preregistered contamination summary reported zero flagged pairs but residual uncertainty remains.
